_note: PARAPHRASED summaries of provisions of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the EU AI Act), written by the project author for retrieval. They are NOT the official text and are not legal advice. Verify every reference against the official text on EUR-Lex before relying on it.

provisions.title: Subliminal or manipulative techniques
provisions.summary: AI that uses subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques to materially distort behaviour and cause or likely cause significant harm.

provisions.title: Exploiting vulnerabilities
provisions.summary: AI that exploits vulnerabilities due to age, disability or social or economic situation to materially distort behaviour and cause significant harm.

provisions.title: Social scoring
provisions.summary: AI that evaluates or classifies people over time based on social behaviour or personality traits, leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment in unrelated contexts or that is unjustified or disproportionate.

provisions.title: Criminal offence risk prediction from profiling alone
provisions.summary: AI that assesses or predicts the risk that a person will commit a criminal offence based solely on profiling or personality traits, not on objective facts linked to criminal activity.

provisions.title: Untargeted facial image scraping
provisions.summary: AI that builds or expands facial recognition databases through untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage.

provisions.title: Emotion recognition at work or in education
provisions.summary: AI that infers emotions of people in the workplace or in education institutions, except for medical or safety reasons.

provisions.title: Biometric categorisation of sensitive attributes
provisions.summary: AI that categorises people from biometric data to infer race, political opinions, trade union membership, religion, sex life or sexual orientation.

provisions.title: Real-time remote biometric identification in public for law enforcement
provisions.summary: Real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement, except in narrowly defined cases with safeguards (for example searching for specific victims, preventing a specific imminent threat, or locating suspects of serious crimes).

provisions.title: Safety component of regulated products
provisions.summary: AI that is a safety component of a product, or is itself a product, covered by EU product-safety legislation listed in Annex I (for example medical devices, machinery, toys, lifts, radio equipment) and that needs a third-party conformity assessment.

provisions.title: Biometrics (remote identification, categorisation, emotion recognition)
provisions.summary: Remote biometric identification systems (not mere verification), biometric categorisation by sensitive or protected attributes, and emotion recognition systems that are not prohibited.

provisions.title: Critical infrastructure
provisions.summary: AI used as a safety component in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or the supply of water, gas, heating and electricity.

provisions.title: Education and vocational training
provisions.summary: AI used to decide access or admission to education, evaluate learning outcomes, assess the appropriate level of education for a person, or monitor and detect prohibited behaviour of students during tests.

provisions.title: Employment and worker management
provisions.summary: AI used for recruitment and selection (targeted job ads, filtering applications, evaluating candidates), and for decisions on work terms, promotion, termination, task allocation based on behaviour or personal traits, and monitoring and evaluating performance.

provisions.title: Eligibility for public benefits and services
provisions.summary: AI used by public authorities to evaluate eligibility for essential public assistance benefits and services, including healthcare, or to grant, reduce, revoke or reclaim them.

provisions.title: Creditworthiness and credit scoring
provisions.summary: AI used to evaluate the creditworthiness of people or establish their credit score, except for detecting financial fraud.

provisions.title: Life and health insurance risk and pricing
provisions.summary: AI used for risk assessment and pricing in relation to life and health insurance.

provisions.title: Emergency calls, dispatch and patient triage
provisions.summary: AI used to evaluate and classify emergency calls, dispatch or prioritise emergency first response services (police, firefighters, medical aid), and emergency healthcare patient triage systems.

provisions.title: Law enforcement
provisions.summary: AI used by or for law enforcement to assess the risk of becoming a victim, as polygraphs and similar tools, to evaluate the reliability of evidence, to assess the risk of offending or re-offending (not solely by profiling), or for profiling in investigations.

provisions.title: Migration, asylum and border control
provisions.summary: AI used by authorities as polygraphs, to assess risks posed by people entering a country (security, irregular migration, health), to examine asylum, visa and residence applications, or to detect and identify people (excluding verification of travel documents).

provisions.title: Justice and democratic processes
provisions.summary: AI used by judicial authorities to research and interpret facts and law and apply the law to facts, and AI intended to influence the outcome of elections or referendums or voting behaviour (not tools for logistics of campaigns).

provisions.title: Chatbots and AI that interacts with people
provisions.summary: Providers must design AI systems that interact directly with people so that people are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious to a reasonably informed person.

provisions.title: Marking of synthetic content
provisions.summary: Providers of AI systems that generate synthetic audio, image, video or text must mark outputs in a machine-readable format so they can be detected as artificially generated or manipulated.

provisions.title: Emotion recognition and biometric categorisation notice
provisions.summary: Deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation systems must inform the people exposed to them.

provisions.title: Deepfakes and AI-generated public-interest text
provisions.summary: Deployers must disclose that image, audio or video content is a deepfake, and disclose AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest, unless the text went through human review or editorial control.

provisions.title: Exception: Annex III systems that are not high-risk
provisions.summary: An Annex III system is not high-risk if it poses no significant risk and only performs a narrow procedural task, improves the result of a previously completed human activity, detects decision-making patterns or deviations without replacing or influencing the human assessment, or does a preparatory task. This exception never applies if the system profiles people.

provisions.title: Other AI systems (minimal risk)
provisions.summary: AI systems not covered by a prohibited practice, high-risk category or transparency duty, such as spam filters, game AI, stock optimisation, grammar checkers, recommendation engines and predictive maintenance that is not a safety component. No specific obligations; voluntary codes of conduct are encouraged.

provisions.title: Exclusion: military, defence and national security
provisions.summary: The Act does not apply to AI systems placed on the market or used exclusively for military, defence or national security purposes.

provisions.title: Exclusion: scientific research and pre-market development
provisions.summary: The Act does not apply to AI systems and models developed and put into service solely for scientific research, or to research, testing and development activity before systems are placed on the market or put into service.

provisions.title: Exclusion: purely personal non-professional use
provisions.summary: The Act does not apply to obligations of people who use AI systems in the course of a purely personal, non-professional activity.
